title: Durable Harness workflows, observations and Linux integrations

rows.capability: Harness lifecycle: open, models/registry/settings/environment, root and close
rows.operation: Open a Harness over a Storage with a Models collection, Registry, resolved settings and optional environment/report sink; obtain the lazily created root; close without losing committed state.
rows.consumer: Independent durable callers and the durable examples; the ordinary coding-agent Session is not this consumer.

scenarios: a scripted model drives admission, one real injected tool, committed entries and final settlement
close and reopen keeps conversations, fork identity, agent choices and provider state

rows.cppSeam: No `cch_durable` target or Harness type exists. `src/coding_agent/runtime/SessionFactory.*` assembles an application AgentSession; `src/agent/harness/RuntimeRoot.*` is the agent executor root.
rows.cppEvidence: `tests/coding_agent/runtime/SessionLifecycleTest.cpp` and `SessionFactory` cover application Session assembly, not a public durable Harness lifecycle. `Harness.open` has no C++ analogue.
rows.recommendation: Create the cch_durable Owner target with a public Harness value owning Storage/Registry/settings/environment lifetime and a root factory. Keep SessionFactory out of cch_durable; do not implement Harness as another AgentSession wrapper.
blockers: no cch_durable target or public Harness implementation

rows.operation: Resolve `toolExecution`, `steeringMode`, `followUpMode`, retry, compaction, progress, contextRetentionMs and documentRetentionMs over their documented defaults, with partial object overrides merged.
rows.consumer: Harness request assembly, generation/compaction policy, observation retention.
rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/SettingsManager.*` and `AgentSessionImpl.hpp` resolve application settings/retry/compaction. There is no durable settings value or document-retention policy.
rows.cppEvidence: `SettingsManagerTest`/`AgentSessionCompactionTest` cover application-level settings; no C++ type represents the durable `Settings` bundle or the document/context retention split.
rows.recommendation: Publish a passive durable Settings value with the upstream defaults and object-merge rules. Capture the default and overridden values through public Harness behavior before marking this row verified.
blockers: no public scenario captured for the complete default/merge matrix

rows.capability: Built-in durable documents: agent, inbox, live, provider and usage
rows.operation: Create the five conversation-scoped built-in documents in the root transaction, expose typed document initial/state, and preserve their state through reopen.
rows.consumer: Harness internals, views, usage aggregation, provider continuity and application adapters.

scenarios: the root conversation is created lazily in one commit with its five built-in documents
close and reopen keeps conversations, fork identity, agent choices and provider state

rows.cppSeam: SessionStore has typed SessionEntry kinds (message/model/thinking/label/compaction/session_info/leaf/custom). `TaskStore` stores task/submission rows. There is no durable document store, document scope/history/fork contract, or the five built-in documents.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionStoreTest.cpp`/`SessionTreeTest.cpp` cover session entries and topology. `SqliteSessionStoreTest.cpp` covers inbox items, but not a generic document model or provider/usage documents.
rows.recommendation: Implement the generic document descriptor/scope/history/fork machinery behind cch_durable, then declare Agent/Inbox/Live/Provider/Usage. Do not overload SessionEntry custom entries as the durable document contract.

rows.operation: Publish one atomic committed change set per transaction, including document creations/changes and entries, so observers see the same commit identity and rewindable state.
rows.consumer: Views, inspection, application adapters and test observers.

scenarios: the root conversation is created lazily in one commit with its five built-in documents

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::subscribe`/`subscribe_session` publish agent and session events after the application assembles them; `SessionEventCommitment` serializes event persistence. They are not a durable commit subscription with document change records.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionEventCommitmentTest.cpp` covers ordered event commitment. No public transaction publication includes document creates/changes.
rows.recommendation: Expose commit publications from the durable transaction seam, with stable commit sequence and typed changes. Reuse the existing event commitment ordering discipline only as an implementation reference, not as the public contract.

rows.operation: Create a conversation with ownerless, conversation or task ownership; return its ID; address it through the Harness; reject inadmissible ownership atomically.
rows.consumer: Task-created subagents, forks, callers and task graph observation.

scenarios: a task-created conversation records its task owner and stays addressable by ID

rows.cppSeam: `SessionStore` creates/opens application sessions; `DurableTask.owner_session` and `TaskStore` associate tasks with sessions. No public conversation owner value covers ownerless/conversation/task ownership or rejects inadmissible ownership in a transaction.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionForkTest.cpp`, `TaskStoreTest.cpp` cover application session and task linkage separately; no durable conversation ownership API.
rows.recommendation: Add a durable ConversationId/ownership value and transaction-validated create/lookup. Keep application SessionStore identity separate until the owner migration starts in cch_durable.

rows.capability: Fork as of an entry with as-of agent state
rows.operation: Fork a conversation at an entry, copy entries/docs as of that entry, preserve ownerless or supplied ownership, and leave the source independent.
rows.consumer: Branch exploration, handoff and durable subagents.

scenarios: a fork copies the transcript and agent state as of its entry and stays independent

rows.cppSeam: `SessionFork.cpp:prepare_fork`, `SessionStore::create_from_entries` and `AgentSession::prepare_fork` copy a branch of the application session tree; there is no durable document-as-of copy or durable fork transaction.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionForkTest.cpp` covers application session forking and entry selection. No durable AgentDoc.asOf or document fork test exists.
rows.recommendation: Reuse the application branch-selection algorithms only as an implementation reference; implement durable fork over the document/transaction store so rewindable docs are copied atomically.

rows.operation: Append a reset marker whose head is itself, carry optional handoff text, and build the subsequent context from the handoff plus later entries.
rows.consumer: Session reset/handoff flows and context rebuilds.

scenarios: reset starts a new context and carries its handoff text as the first user message

rows.cppSeam: `SessionStore::reset_leaf` only moves the application active leaf to the root; there is no reset entry carrying handoff text, and `SessionTree::buildSessionContext` has no reset semantics.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionStoreTest.cpp`/`SessionTreeTest.cpp` cover leaf movement and branch context, not durable reset/handoff.
rows.recommendation: Represent reset as a durable entry with self-head and optional handoff content; rebuild context from it rather than reusing the leaf-reset application behavior.
blockers: no durable reset entry or handoff context

rows.operation: Abort a busy conversation, cancel the active generation, settle the placed input unanswered with an explicit reason, clear live state and leave no live task.
rows.consumer: Interactive abort, cancellation and recovery callers.

scenarios: conversation abort stops the busy generation and settles its input unanswered

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::abort` cancels an application prompt; `TaskScheduler::request_abort` marks durable tasks. There is no durable conversation-to-submission settlement path.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionCloseTest.cpp` covers cancellation through close; `TaskSchedulerTest.cpp` covers task abort. The caller-visible unanswered submission settlement is not implemented.
rows.recommendation: Connect conversation abort to the durable submission/generation task through one transaction and expose the unanswered reason. Keep AgentSession abort as application-only behavior.

rows.capability: Reopen conversations, forks and provider state
rows.operation: Close and reopen a Harness over durable storage; recover root/child/fork identity, agent choices, provider session identity and transcript.
rows.consumer: Restart recovery and long-lived durable callers.

scenarios: close and reopen keeps conversations, fork identity, agent choices and provider state

rows.cppSeam: `SessionStore::create_sqlite`/`open_sqlite`, `SessionResume` and `SessionFork` recover application conversations and model/thinking metadata. No durable document/provider/usage recovery exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `SqliteSessionStoreTest.cpp` covers commit/reopen and tree replay; `SessionResume` tests cover active-path history. No durable Harness reopen test.
rows.recommendation: Implement durable reopen over the document/task store and prove it at the public Harness boundary; do not use session-file resume as the durable storage continuation proof.

rows.capability: Generation admission, entries and caller-visible settlement
rows.operation: Admit an input submission, run a generation task, commit user/system/assistant entries, execute tool rounds and settle done/error/aborted with entry and answer identities.

scenarios: a scripted model drives admission, one real injected tool, committed entries and final settlement
a generation onYield hook appends a user message and continues the same admitted run

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::prompt`/`AgentSessionExecution` run application turns; `TaskScheduler` can persist a handler task but no GenerationTask type, submission admission or durable settlement receipt exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionLifecycleTest.cpp`/`SessionCloseTest.cpp` cover application turns and close. No durable submission admission or generation task test.
rows.recommendation: Make generation a durable task that writes one terminal receipt and commits entries/tool tasks transactionally. Keep application prompt execution out of the durable task identity.
blockers: no durable GenerationTask or submission receipt

rows.operation: Append a retryable provider error, retry the same run up to maxRetries with the configured delay, and settle with the eventual answer; overflow is not a retry.

scenarios: a retryable provider error is appended and the same run retries to a completed answer

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSessionExecution.cpp` implements application turn auto-retry and emits auto_retry events; the policy is application settings, not a durable GenerationTask state with persisted retry deadline.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentSessionCompactionTest.cpp`/`AgentSessionExecution` retry tests cover application retry behavior; no durable retry-state recovery test.
rows.recommendation: Persist retry attempt/deadline in the generation checkpoint and reuse the existing error classification only behind the durable task. Prove replay after reopen.

rows.capability: Request prompt and tool context assembly
rows.operation: Assemble the system prompt sections and offered/callable/deferred tools from the current registry and agent choices for each model request.
rows.consumer: Generation task, extension authors and application adapters.

scenarios: a registry install after conversation creation changes the next request's tools and prompt sections
a blocking threshold compaction appends its summary before the request it protects

rows.cppSeam: `SystemPromptBuilder.*`, `ToolRegistry` and `AgentSession` assemble application prompts and tool lists. No durable section registry, agent selection or per-request prompt snapshot exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `SystemPromptBuilder` tests and `SessionAssemblyContractTest.cpp` cover application prompt/tool assembly. No durable prompt-section or deferred/callable split test.
rows.recommendation: Use a passive durable agent/selection value and render sections from the registry snapshot at each request. Do not route the durable prompt through the application SystemPromptBuilder.

rows.capability: Steering and follow-up queue admission modes
rows.operation: Queue steering/follow-up input with one-at-a-time or all modes, drain in the configured order, and settle/reject at capacity as upstream does.
rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::steer`, `follow_up`, `set_steering_mode`, `clear_*` implement application queues; durable submission admission modes and capacity behavior are absent.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentSession` input-queue tests cover application steering/follow-up mutations. No durable queue-mode or admission test.
rows.recommendation: Model steering/follow-up as durable submissions or inbox items with the upstream drain modes; capture the busy/idle outcomes before verification.
blockers: no public scenario captured for durable steering/follow-up

rows.operation: Summarize eligible old history for a manual compact request, retain raw history, append one compaction marker at the cut, place it as a done submission and rebuild context.

scenarios: manual compaction summarizes old context, keeps raw history, and places one summary marker at the cut

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::compact` plus `harness::session::compact` implement application compaction and persist a CompactionEntry. There is no durable compaction task, marker entry, placement submission or document-aware retained tail.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentSessionCompactionTest.cpp` and `tests/coding_agent/compaction/CompactionTest.cpp` cover manual compaction and context rebuild. They use application session entries, not the durable compaction task/submission contract.
rows.recommendation: Build a durable CompactionTask over the durable context/entry model; place its marker as a submission and keep the raw entries. Reuse the summarization stream seam, not the application entry schema.

rows.capability: Blocking threshold compaction before a request
rows.operation: When the next request would exceed the threshold, compact synchronously before sending it, append the marker ahead of the request and continue with the protected request.

scenarios: a blocking threshold compaction appends its summary before the request it protects

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSessionCompaction.cpp` performs application threshold/overflow checks and rebuilds context. There is no durable background/threshold task split or persisted checkpoint.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentSessionCompactionTest.cpp` covers threshold compaction and between-turn behavior; no durable threshold task.
rows.recommendation: Place the threshold decision in the durable generation checkpoint and persist the compaction child task before the protected request. Verify the marker ordering after reopen.

rows.capability: Background compaction without blocking a run
rows.operation: Start compaction above the background threshold without blocking the run; idle waits and Esc ignore it; the result is placed when it finishes.
rows.consumer: Long-running durable conversations and interactive clients.
rows.cppSeam: Application compaction is synchronous within the AgentSession turn; there is no detached background task, idle wait or Esc-ignore semantics.
rows.cppEvidence: No C++ test represents detached background compaction or its cancellation/placement behavior.
rows.recommendation: Implement compaction as a normal durable child task with background placement policy; capture the non-blocking run and idle/Esc interaction in a dedicated public scenario.
blockers: no background compaction scenario or implementation

rows.operation: Invoke a beforeCompact hook before the cut; a `{decline:true}` result leaves history uncompacted and sends the request uncompacted.

scenarios: a compaction beforeCompact hook can decline the cut and the request goes out uncompacted

rows.cppSeam: There is no durable compaction hook dispatcher. Application Agent lifecycle hooks do not expose a beforeCompact decision.
rows.cppEvidence: No C++ beforeCompact decline seam or test.
rows.recommendation: Dispatch durable compaction hooks from the task checkpoint before preparation and persist the decline decision; do not model it as an exception.

rows.operation: On a context-overflow error, compact old history once, retry the same request, and fail explicitly on a second overflow.
rows.cppSeam: `AgentSessionCompaction.cpp` implements application compact-and-retry-once with the upstream recovery text. No durable generation checkpoint or retry-once state exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentSessionCompactionTest.cpp` covers overflow compact-and-retry and the second-overflow error.
rows.recommendation: Reuse the error classification and compaction task in the durable generation checkpoint, and prove the retry-once outcome after reopen.

rows.operation: Complete a compaction request without a summary or marker when there is no eligible cut, preserving the context.
rows.consumer: Callers compacting small or already-compacted conversations.

scenarios: manual compaction with no eligible cut completes without a summary or a marker

rows.cppSeam: `harness::session::compact` returns CompactionSkipped with Empty/AlreadyCompacted/NothingToSummarize; `AgentSession::compact` surfaces application errors/results. Durable no-cut completion is absent.
rows.cppEvidence: `tests/coding_agent/compaction/CompactionTest.cpp` covers skip reasons at the application door.
rows.recommendation: Return the typed skip outcome through the durable task terminal result without writing a compaction entry; keep it distinct from a failed task.

rows.operation: Install or replace an extension after conversation creation and have the next request see its tools and prompt sections; uninstall removes it.
rows.consumer: Extension hosts, durable callers and tool selection.

scenarios: a registry install after conversation creation changes the next request's tools and prompt sections
close and reopen keeps conversations, fork identity, agent choices and provider state

rows.cppSeam: `ToolRegistry`/`ExtensionToolRegistry` and `SessionFactory` assemble application tools/extensions. There is no public durable registry snapshot (tools, sections, tasks) or subscription-driven scheduler wakeup.
rows.cppEvidence: `ExtensionToolSourceTest.cpp` and `SessionAssemblyContractTest.cpp` cover application extension tool registration. No durable registry snapshot/live transition test.
rows.recommendation: Publish an immutable durable registry snapshot with tools/sections/task definitions and subscribe the scheduler to publications. Keep application extension loading separate.

rows.capability: Task definitions and versioned handler resolution
rows.operation: Install task definitions by name/version, resolve them at reservation and at each phase boundary, replace a future definition, and block missing/older definitions honestly.

scenarios: inspect derives ready, running, waiting and blocked task states without running task code
the task graph follows owner edges, owned conversations, waits and completion to empty

rows.cppSeam: `TaskScheduler::register_handler` registers a single `std::function<Expected<std::string>(std::stop_token)>`; `TaskStore` stores kind/version. No typed initial/phases/abort/migrate definition or phase-boundary resolution exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `TaskSchedulerTest.cpp` covers future-definition replacement, version regression, recovery and missing handlers. The public evidence scenarios use the frozen typed definitions, not a C++ equivalent.
rows.recommendation: Add a typed task-definition value and resolve it by kind/version at each reservation/phase boundary. Keep the handler adapter as an implementation detail.

rows.operation: Render extension sections and agent instructions into the system prompt at the correct ordering, including sections added after conversation creation.

scenarios: a registry install after conversation creation changes the next request's tools and prompt sections
a blocking threshold compaction appends its summary before the request it protects

rows.cppSeam: `SystemPromptBuilder` and `ProjectResourceLoader` assemble application prompt sections/instructions. There is no durable section registry or per-request extension section order.
rows.cppEvidence: `SystemPromptBuilder` tests and `SessionAssemblyContractTest.cpp` cover application sections. No durable section ordering test.
rows.recommendation: Render durable extension sections from the registry snapshot with explicit reserved-key ordering; do not reuse application prompt templates as the durable contract.

rows.operation: Invoke an onYield hook with the assistant message; `{continue: text}` appends a user message and continues the same admitted generation, ending at the second answer.

scenarios: a generation onYield hook appends a user message and continues the same admitted run

rows.cppSeam: `Agent`/`AgentSession` expose lifecycle observers and steering/follow-up queues, not a durable generation hook that mutates the checkpoint continuation.
rows.cppEvidence: No C++ generation onYield continuation test; Agent observer tests are application event subscriptions.
rows.recommendation: Dispatch the hook at the generation checkpoint, persist the continuation as a user entry and keep one submission receipt. Prove the call count and transcript.

rows.operation: Invoke beforeTool before execution (allowing argument replacement) and afterTool with the result, preserving the final committed tool result and entry.

scenarios: tool hooks rewrite arguments before execution and observe the committed result

rows.cppSeam: Agent tool policy hooks (before/after-tool policies) exist in the application Agent loop; there is no durable ToolTask hook registry or hook/result persistence contract.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentBehaviorTest` covers application before/after-tool policy cancellation and transforms; no durable ToolTask hook test.
rows.recommendation: Dispatch durable tool hooks around the ToolTask execution and persist the committed result once. Keep application policy hooks separate.

rows.capability: Native extension run triggering and busy-state hooks
rows.operation: Expose native C++ registration, tool wrapping, run triggering and prompt/busy-state lifecycle hooks as selected by ADR 0075.
rows.consumer: Native extension authors and application/durable adapters.
rows.cppSeam: Application Agent lifecycle observers and tool policies exist, but no native extension registration/run-triggering surface or durable busy-state hook contract exists.
rows.cppEvidence: Application observer/policy tests exist; no native C++ extension hook inventory or durable run-trigger test.
rows.recommendation: Separate the native extension seam from TypeScript plugin execution; implement the selected hooks as C++ values and prove registration, wrapping and run triggering.

rows.operation: Inspect scheduling and tasks without running task code: ready, running, waiting (with dependencies), blocked (with reason), completed and terminal state.

scenarios: inspect derives ready, running, waiting and blocked task states without running task code
inspect lists the placed submission and the generation task that owns it

rows.cppSeam: `TaskStore::recover_tasks`/`load_task` and `TaskScheduler` expose flat rows; no public `inspect` result, scheduling state, dependency/waiting state or missing-definition blocked reason exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `TaskStoreTest.cpp`/`TaskSchedulerTest.cpp` cover recovery/transition states, but no inspection projection.
rows.recommendation: Implement an inspect projection over the durable store/scheduler that never executes task code; include submission placement and blocked reasons.

rows.operation: List placed submissions with conversation identity, type and status while a generation is busy; status and task ownership stay consistent with `submission.status`.

scenarios: inspect lists the placed submission and the generation task that owns it

rows.cppSeam: `TaskStore` stores TaskSubmission request IDs/state. There is no public inspection API and no conversation-scoped submission status projection.
rows.cppEvidence: `TaskStoreTest.cpp` covers submission dedup across reopen; no placed-submission inspection test.
rows.recommendation: Expose placed submissions and their generation task in the durable inspect result; keep the store row private.

rows.operation: Observe tasks by owner edges and live state, owned conversations, dependency waits and completion to an empty graph; dispose the view.

scenarios: the task graph follows owner edges, owned conversations, waits and completion to empty

rows.cppSeam: No task graph view exists. `TaskStore` has parent_task_id/owner_session/descendants, but no public graph projection or owned-conversation join.
rows.cppEvidence: `TaskStoreTest.cpp` covers descendants and ownership; no graph view.
rows.recommendation: Build the graph projection over task/ownership/live-document state; do not add a second scheduler state store.

rows.operation: Watch a conversation and receive ordered patch/delta frames whose final value equals a fresh hydration, including entries and built-in documents.

scenarios: conversation watch publishes delta frames whose final view equals a fresh hydration

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::snapshot` plus ordered PatchMsg projection and `subscribe` provide application observation. No durable viewState/watch/delta semantics or document hydration exists.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentSessionSnapshotTest.cpp`/`SessionEventCommitmentTest.cpp` cover application snapshots and ordered patches; no durable view/watch test.
rows.recommendation: Implement durable view hydration and delta frames over commit publications; keep application projection messages out of the durable API.

rows.operation: Stream run/turn/message/tool/usage/submission events in order, with tool start/update/end and result entry linkage, and stop the stream cleanly.

scenarios: the agent event stream reports run, turn, message, tool and submission lifecycle in order

rows.cppSeam: `AgentSession::subscribe`/`subscribe_session` emit application Agent/session events; there is no durable AgentEvent vocabulary or watch stream tied to durable entries/submissions.
rows.cppEvidence: Application event/observer tests cover lifecycle ordering; no durable event stream test.
rows.recommendation: Map the agent event seam into durable event records and prove ordering/tool result linkage at the durable stream. Do not claim the application event stream is the durable stream.

rows.capability: Context as of an entry and fork-start equivalence
rows.operation: Read a conversation context at an entry cursor with entries/messages/head, and show a fork would start from the same committed view.
rows.consumer: Fork preparation, context inspection and replay.

scenarios: context with an entry cursor returns the same committed view a fork would start from

rows.cppSeam: `SessionStore::build_context` and `get_branch` build an application active-path context; there is no durable entry-cursor context API or document-as-of context.
rows.cppEvidence: `SessionTreeTest.cpp`/`SessionResume` tests cover application branch context; no durable context-at-entry test.
rows.recommendation: Share the branch/cut selection implementation with durable fork and context; expose entries/messages/head as passive values.

rows.operation: Track per-conversation model/tool usage in the usage document and expose increased input usage after a summarization request.

scenarios: manual compaction summarizes old context, keeps raw history, and places one summary marker at the cut
the root conversation is created lazily in one commit with its five built-in documents

rows.cppSeam: `ai::Usage` and AgentSession usage events exist; TaskStore/session entries do not provide a durable UsageDoc aggregation.
rows.cppEvidence: Application usage accounting tests exist in AgentSession/ModelRuntime; no durable UsageDoc aggregate test.
rows.recommendation: Implement the usage document as a normal durable document and update it transactionally with generation/summary usage.

rows.capability: Submission deduplication, inbox admission and queue modes
rows.operation: Deduplicate submissions by request ID, place/queue by conversation state, apply one-at-a-time/all modes, and keep inbox/live documents consistent.
rows.cppSeam: `TaskStore::submit/load_submission` deduplicates request IDs; `AgentSession` has steering/follow-up/inbox queues. No durable submission placement/inbox/live contract ties them together.
rows.cppEvidence: `TaskStoreTest.cpp` covers submission dedup; AgentSession input queue tests cover application queue behavior. No durable queue-mode/inbox scenario.
rows.recommendation: The evidence for this row is owned by A10; do not duplicate its scenarios here. Implement durable admission once and have Harness inspect/view consume it.
blockers: no public durable admission scenario in this bundle; A10 evidence remains upstream-only for this lane

rows.operation: Open a SQLite database, commit conversations/entries/docs/tasks atomically, close, reopen and continue with the same identities and state.

scenarios: close and reopen keeps conversations, fork identity, agent choices and provider state

rows.cppSeam: `SqliteSessionStore`/`SqliteDatabase` and `TaskStore` use a SQLite schema, but it is the application session/task schema, not the pi-durable document/main/sidecar contract. Bidirectional frozen-pi opening is not implemented.
rows.cppEvidence: `SqliteSessionStoreTest.cpp` and `TaskStoreTest.cpp` cover atomic application commits/reopen. No bidirectional pi-durable SQLite test.
rows.recommendation: A10 owns the storage format evidence and bidirectional checks; cch_durable must consume that contract. Do not treat application SQLite persistence as durable format parity.

rows.operation: Write pi-durable main/sidecar JSONL, reopen and continue with committed state; preserve document/task recovery semantics.

scenarios: JSONL storage writes its files and reopens the same conversation and transcript

rows.cppSeam: `JsonlSessionStore` is the application coding-agent transcript format, not pi-durable main/sidecar storage. It cannot open/continue frozen durable JSONL.
rows.cppEvidence: `JsonlSessionStoreTest.cpp` covers application JSONL append/reload; no durable main/sidecar test.
rows.recommendation: Implement the durable JSONL main/sidecar codec and recovery, then run bidirectional continuation with frozen pi. Keep application transcript JSONL separate.
blockers: no pi-durable JSONL format or bidirectional test

rows.capability: Task persistence, recovery and abort ownership
rows.operation: Persist task kind/version/checkpoint/owner/submission, recover after restart, resume only registered definitions, and cascade abort through owned descendants.
rows.consumer: Durable scheduler, crash recovery and task authors.

scenarios: the task graph follows owner edges, owned conversations, waits and completion to empty
inspect derives ready, running, waiting and blocked task states without running task code

rows.cppSeam: `TaskStore`/`TaskScheduler` implement flat durable tasks, checkpoints, recovery and abort descendants. They lack typed definitions, structured outcomes, documents, task graph and inspection.
rows.cppEvidence: `TaskStoreTest.cpp`/`TaskSchedulerTest.cpp` cover the existing flat contract thoroughly. A10 evidence covers submissions/inbox/recovery in more depth.
rows.recommendation: Migrate the existing store/scheduler behind the cch_durable task contract rather than extending the flat handler API in place.
blockers: typed task contract and structured outcomes missing

rows.operation: Read/write/append/list/stat/remove/temp operations, path resolution, missing-file errors and cleanup over a real local Linux directory.
rows.consumer: Durable tools, images and code-mode output files.

scenarios: the real Node ExecutionEnv reads, appends, lists, executes split streams and reports timeout

rows.cppSeam: `WorkspaceFileSystem.*`, `AsyncLocalFileSystem.*`, `LocalFileSystem.hpp` implement application filesystem operations and path resolution.
rows.cppEvidence: `src/agent/harness/Workspace*` tests cover application filesystem behavior; no durable ExecutionEnv value API or temp/cleanup contract.
rows.recommendation: Publish an ExecutionEnv interface and a local Linux adapter for cch_durable; reuse the safe path/atomic-write mechanics without exposing application Session ownership.

rows.capability: Local shell execution, split output and timeout
rows.operation: Execute string and argv commands, stream stdout/stderr separately, return exit codes, honor timeout/abort and spill output.
rows.consumer: Built-in bash tool, code mode and durable callers.

scenarios: the real Node ExecutionEnv reads, appends, lists, executes split streams and reports timeout

rows.cppSeam: `AsyncLocalShell.*`, `LocalShell.hpp`, `Process.*` and `ShellResolver.*` implement application shell execution with streaming and cancellation.
rows.cppEvidence: Application shell tests cover execution; no durable ExecutionEnv shell result/timeout contract.
rows.recommendation: Extract the local process mechanics behind the durable ExecutionEnv value; prove split streams, timeout and abort in the durable adapter.

rows.capability: Built-in read/write/edit/bash tools over an injected environment
rows.operation: Offer real read/write/edit/bash tools, execute them with the conversation environment, commit tool results with call IDs/errors and continue the model turn.
rows.consumer: Durable agent callers and code mode nested tools.

scenarios: the built-in read, write, edit and bash tools run over a real injected local environment

rows.cppSeam: `agent::tools::create_*_tool`/`AsyncToolFactories.cpp` provide application tools over abstract filesystem/shell; they are assembled by the application, not cch_durable.
rows.cppEvidence: `AgentToolSurfaceTest.cpp` and tool tests cover application tools. The durable `createCodingTools()` extension and environment injection are absent.
rows.recommendation: Move the concrete tool implementations to the durable owner or a shared contract without making cch_durable depend on cch_coding_agent; keep application tool policy separate.

rows.operation: Prepare inline images for a model within byte/dimension limits, pass an upright inline image through, resize over-limit images, map coordinates and return undefined for invalid data.
rows.consumer: Read tool, image input and durable callers.

scenarios: the Photon image processor passes an upright inline image through and resizes one over the limits

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/ImageInput.*` processes image input with STB/WebP decode, EXIF orientation and coordinate hints; it is application-owned and uses different decoding mechanics.
rows.cppEvidence: `ImageInputTest.cpp` covers resizing/orientation/coordinate hints and invalid WebP omission; no durable ImageProcessor interface or Photon parity.
rows.recommendation: Implement the durable ImageProcessor contract with local Linux decoding; keep model/provider image execution limited to the retained Magpie capabilities.

rows.capability: Read tool image content and coordinate diagnostic
rows.operation: Read a supported inline image, return the image content block plus a diagnostic with resize/coordinate mapping, and preserve model-visible behavior.
rows.consumer: Durable read tool and vision-capable callers.

scenarios: the read tool returns a resized image content block with its coordinate-mapping diagnostic
